jobs.title: Field Technician
jobs.description:
Astro Pak
is the nation's leading precision cleaning and passivation contractor specializing in on-site cleaning of high purity gas and fluid systems, as well as precision cleaning of components and hardware at the company’s Cleanroom facilities. Astro Pak
provides services to over 15 sectors including: Data Centers, Biotechnology, Pharmaceutical, Aerospace, Semiconductor, and other selected Industrial markets. The company, founded in 1959, has performed on-site precision chemical cleaning in every State of the Union as well as several projects in Asia, Canada, continental Europe, England, Ireland and Mexico.

Astro Pak is looking for motivated individuals who want more than a typical job. As an Associate Field Technician
, you’ll travel to cutting-edge facilities across the country while learning a specialized technical trade used in industries like aerospace, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, and advanced manufacturing.

If you enjoy hands-on work, solving problems, and seeing new places while building valuable technical skills, this role could be a great fit.

$3,000 Sign-On Bonus********

What You’ll Experience

This is not a typical entry-level job. It’s a traveling technical career path
.

You’ll receive immersive training and work alongside experienced technicians performing specialized chemical cleaning and passivation on mission-critical fluid and gas systems.

Every project is different. One week you may be working at a semiconductor facility, the next supporting aerospace manufacturing.

Expect

Extensive travel to project sites across the U.S.
Hands-on work with specialized equipment and chemical processes
Rapid skill development and certifications
Opportunities to grow into senior technician or leadership roles

Travel Requirements

80%+ travel nationwide
30–50% night shift work
Overtime, weekends, holidays, and short-notice travel may be required

What You’ll Do

As part of a field service team, you will:

Set up and operate specialized equipment for chemical cleaning and passivation
Safely handle process chemicals such as citric acid and caustics
Use PPE and follow strict safety and compliance procedures
Load, transport, and unload project equipment and materials
Drive company vehicles to job sites (vans, trucks, forklifts)
Perform hands-on work in a variety of environments (indoors, outdoors, rooftops)
Maintain organized workspaces aligned with 5S/CEO standards
Complete OSHA and internal safety training
Support mission-critical customer facilities across the country

Who Thrives In This Role

We hire for attitude and train for success.

The Best Candidates Are

Mechanically inclined
Comfortable working with tools and equipment
Adaptable to new environments
Safety-focused
Excited about travel and hands-on work
Interested in building a long-term technical career

Basic Requirements

Valid Class C driver’s license with clean driving record
Real ID or Passport required for air travel
Ability to attend two weeks of paid training in California within the first 3 weeks of employment
Medical DOT certificate
Strong math skills (ratios, percentages)
Comfortable using mobile technology and basic programs (Word, Excel, Outlook)
Fluent in English with strong communication skills
Ability to lift 50 lbs. and work in PPE in changing environments
Willingness to work night shifts, overtime, weekends, and holidays

Preferred (But Not Required)

High School Diploma or GED
Technical schooling or trade certification
OSHA / HAZWOPER / Confined Space certifications
Field service or hazardous chemical handling experience

Why Join Astro Pak?

Paid Training & Certifications

No experience required. We provide hands-on training and help you earn industry certifications.

Travel Opportunities

Work at advanced manufacturing and technology facilities across the country while building your career.

Career Growth

Many of our technicians advance quickly into senior technical roles, trainers, or leadership positions.

Team Culture

Work alongside experienced professionals in a safety-first, supportive team environment.

Competitive Benefits

Highly subsidized medical, dental, and vision insurance
401(k) with company match
Paid time off and family leave
Travel stipend
Training and development opportunities
Flexible spending accounts and more

Compensation:
The pay for this position typically has a starting rate of $20-$21. The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience and location

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst
jobs.description:
About The Role

The Commercial Analytics & DS team is the analytical engine of Hinge Health's commercial business – the team that CS, Partnerships/HSO, and Commercial leadership rely on for the data, metrics, and strategic thinking that drive client retention, program growth, and commercial decision-making. We build the self-service analytics infrastructure, AI-powered workflows, and high-stakes deliverables that define how HH's commercial organization understands and acts on its data.

We are looking for a Senior Data Analyst to serve as the team's senior individual contributor, dedicated AI champion, and organizational thought partner. You will independently own the team's most complex and highest-stakes initiatives – from the CS KPI and partner reporting suite to the commercial dbt data layer to the team's AI and self-service portfolio – and serve as the go-to analytical authority for CS, Commercial, and Partnerships/HSO leadership. AI ownership is a primary mandate, not a side contribution: the foundations are real (a working AFTR workflow, a first-generation Data Discovery Agent, active AnswerBot development), and your job is to take those proof points from promising to compounding. You are technically deep in SQL, dbt, and cloud data platforms – and you use that depth in service of framing strategy and owning methodology, not just executing it. The team operates lean and moves fast. If the role you are imagining requires someone to write tickets and execute – this is not it.

What You'll Accomplish

Strategic Analytics & Commercial Leadership

Serve as the primary analytical thought partner to CS, Commercial, and Partnerships/HSO leadership – owning the framing, scoping, and delivery of high-impact analyses across client retention strategy, surgery intent analytics, program expansion, commercial performance, client health, and performance guarantee reporting
Own and maintain the CS KPI and Bowler reporting suite – the dashboards and metrics CS leadership depends on to track commercial performance
Lead multi-quarter analytical initiatives end-to-end with full autonomy; the team's P0 initiatives (Analytics OS, client hub, retention model) should not require the hiring manager to carry them
Navigate complex cross-functional dynamics: manage stakeholder relationships without authority, push back constructively when data is being misread, drive alignment on methodology even when it is inconvenient, and absorb organizational friction so the rest of the team can focus on the work

AI Leadership & Self-Service Analytics

Own the team's AI and self-service strategy as the dedicated AI champion for Commercial Analytics – the counterpart to the AI lead role on HH's product-side Data Science team, with equivalent mandate and accountability
Scale and compound the team's existing AI portfolio: the CSM AnswerBot (v2 rebuild in Claude, a recurring stakeholder ask with active external pressure on timelines); the Data Discovery Agent (DDA) (v1 is in production and demonstrates the concept works; v2 must reach the reliability and scale the organization needs); and AFTR (Add Field To Report) v2.0 (proven internally as a meaningful toil-reducer; v2.0's ambition is to surface it directly to stakeholders so they can extend their own reports without analyst involvement)
Drive the team's contribution to the Analytics OS – the long-term platform into which the AnswerBot, DDA, and AFTR are intended to be incorporated; own Commercial Analytics' roadmap within it and ensure the tools you are scaling are being built toward that destination from day one
Use AI-assisted tools (Claude Code, Cursor, and equivalents) actively and with genuine curiosity; bring a real appetite for agentic workflows, and contribute to Matik-powered reporting automation that reduces the team's dependency on manual, recurring analytical requests

Data Modeling & Commercial Infrastructure

Own and evolve the commercial dbt data layer and mesh architecture – keeping it clean, well-tested, and scalable
Drive CDM enhancements including program-specific modeling (migraines, WPH, GI) and user-level pain reporting updates tied to the NRS/VAS transition
Partner with analytics engineers and data engineers to ensure commercial data flows reliably from upstream services into reporting-ready tables; advocate for upstream instrumentation best practices with Engineering partners

Communication, Teaching & Team Elevation

Communicate complexity simply and without condescension – you can explain a data model architecture, a statistical methodology, or a pipeline failure to a CSM, a CS VP, and a data engineer, and the explanation lands differently each time because you know your audience
Uplevel team analytical capability through documentation, structured knowledge transfer, ad hoc coaching, and building shared practices
Mentor through design reviews, analytical critique, and real pairing – actively raising the bar for what good looks like

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field or equivalent professional experience
3+ years of experience as a data analyst with a demonstrated track record of owning complex, cross-functional analytical work in a commercial or product environment
Sufficient technical depth in SQL, Python, and cloud data platforms (Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery, or equivalent) to shape data architecture decisions, scope data model work, and partner credibly with analytics engineers
Experience delivering strategic analytical work to VP+ stakeholders – including framing ambiguous problems, developing methodology under uncertainty, and presenting results to people who will challenge you
Demonstrated ability to drive organizational alignment on data definitions, methodology, or reporting strategy across CS, Product, and engineering stakeholders without relying on formal authority
Deep healthcare industry knowledge – clinical, payer, provider, or digital health; the team's work (concurrent care, clinical outcomes, commercial contracting, payer reporting) demands fluency that only comes from having worked in it

Preferred Qualifications

Experience serving as a dedicated AI champion on an analytics team – not just a power user or early adopter, but someone who has taken existing AI proof points and scaled them into reliable, compounding capabilities that other people depend on; the portfolio here exists and is working – it needs ownership at scale
Track record of communicating analytical complexity to non-technical stakeholders clearly and without jargon – a CFO, a CSM team, and a data engineering team can all understand the same decision and walk away able to act on it
Prior experience building or leading self-service analytics platforms – including the governance, documentation, and training that makes self-service actually work; experience with a unified analytics platform that consolidates multiple tools under a shared architecture
History of mentoring analysts and raising team capability through shared standards, design review, and direct coaching – not just completing deliverables
Background in a lean, high-ownership team where you had to set your own analytical agenda rather than receive it – and a demonstrated preference for operating that way

Location & Hybrid Working Model — San Francisco

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ and follows Hinge Health’s hybrid working model. We believe that remote work and in-person work each have their own advantages, and we want to leverage the best of both worlds. Employees in hybrid roles are required to be in the office 3 days per week, for the full 8 hours of a typical business day. Our San Francisco office also has a dog-friendly workplace program.

About Hinge Health

Hinge Health leverages software, including AI, to largely automate care for joint and muscle health, delivering an outstanding member experience, improved member outcomes, and cost reductions for its clients. The company has designed its platform to address a broad spectrum of MSK care—from acute injury, to chronic pain, to post-surgical rehabilitation—and the platform can help to ease members’ pain, improve their function, and reduce their need for surgeries, all while driving health equity by allowing members to engage in their exercise therapy sessions from anywhere. The company is headquartered in San Francisco, California.

Learn more at http://www.hingehealth.com

What You'll Love About Us

Participation in our Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), allowing you to acquire company stock via payroll at a 15% discount against the lower market price.
Comprehensive and inclusive medical coverage and benefit programs for you and your dependents.
Flexible retirement savings through Traditional or Roth 401(k) investment paths.
Dedicated lifestyle stipends designed to fuel your professional growth and continuous learning.

Culture and Engagement

Hinge Health is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. We make employment decisions without regards to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, veteran status, disability status, pregnancy, or any other basis protected by federal, state or local law. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities. If you feel you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, let us know by reaching out to your recruiter. By submitting your application you are acknowledging we are using your personal data as outlined in the personnel and candidate privacy policy.

Beware of Phishing Attempts: We've noticed an increase in phishing where fraudsters impersonate employees and send fake job offers to steal sensitive information. We'll never ask for financial details during the hiring process and only use "@hingehealth.com" emails. If you receive a suspicious offer, stop communication and report it to the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center. To verify an email from our recruiting team, forward it to security@hingehealth.com.

jobs.description:
Find your path and enjoy the journey at Haley & Aldrich
. With us, you’ll tackle clients’ most meaningful challenges in the built and natural environments – and, in turn, build stronger communities. You’ll work with teams of passionate colleagues, driven by a commitment to technical excellence and continuous learning.

As a company, we aim to build a world where communities go beyond resilience, embracing change as an opportunity to enhance safety, well-being, and quality of life. Join us to accelerate this vision and your professional development.

We are looking to add new talent to our growing team! We are seeking an experienced and accomplished Senior Chemical/Environmental Engineer or Environmental Scientist
3
(specializing in Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) Regulatory Compliance) to lead high-performing teams, cultivate deep client relationships, and deliver innovative solutions. This is an exciting opportunity to play a key leadership role in shaping the future of our business, driving both growth and innovation. The is a full-time
role and based in either our Costa Mesa, CA
or San Diego, CA
office.

In this position, you will have an opportunity to play a key role in delivering strategic value and driving meaningful outcomes for our clients and team. You will act as a seller/doer, developing and maintaining client relationships, leading multi-disciplinary project teams, executing high-quality deliverables, and mentoring junior staff. Your expertise will guide technical execution and proactive compliance strategies, helping clients navigate complex regulations and implement effective EHS programs. If you’re ready to take your career to the next level and contribute to a dynamic and growing company, we’d love to hear from you!

Duties/Responsibilities

In this position, you will:

Lead and grow the company’s portfolio by developing and maintaining strategic client relationships, identifying new business opportunities, and driving significant revenue growth.
Oversee large, complex projects from initiation to completion, ensuring they meet technical, budgetary, and client satisfaction goals. Serve as a senior leader on project teams and oversee all phases of service delivery.
Build and guide high-performance teams, fostering a collaborative environment. Mentor emerging talent and promote staff development through hands-on coaching and leadership during project execution.
Contribute to the company’s long-term strategy by identifying new markets, services, and technologies, and leading proposals for high-impact projects.
Actively participate in professional organizations, representing the company, providing thought leadership, and influencing industry trends.
Ensure that all work is performed in accordance with company and client Health & Safety protocols.
Demonstrate our foundational safety behaviors.
Provide senior technical and strategic leadership for EHS regulatory compliance programs, including RCRA compliance, with an emphasis on clients in California.

Skills/Experience

Minimum Skills and Requirements:

Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, or related field.
15+ years of experience in EHS regulatory compliance, RCRA compliance, or related technical areas, with a proven track record of driving business growth through client relationships and leadership in complex projects.
Demonstrated expertise in both business development and project leadership, with experience safely and profitably leading multiple projects simultaneously and managing client portfolios.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to convey complex ideas and lead client and internal discussions effectively.
Proven leadership experience in building and managing diverse teams, mentoring staff, and fostering collaboration.
Strong business acumen with the ability to balance strategic growth, client needs, and company profitability.

Preferred Skills

Professional registration or certification in a relevant field is preferred, such as PE, CSP, or CIH.
Significant experience in California EHS compliance markets, with established relationships and insights into industry trends.
Experience presenting at conferences, writing articles or contributing thought leadership within professional organizations.
A passion for continuous learning and innovation, staying at the forefront of industry developments.

The salary range for this position in Costa Mesa, CA and San Diego, CA
is $105,000-$170,000
annually
. Actual compensation will be based upon a variety of factors such as education, related work experience, certificates, skills, and current market conditions. Haley & Aldrich reviews salary ranges each quarter to assess competitiveness with the market.

About Haley & Aldrich

Haley & Aldrich is committed to delivering the value our clients need from their capital, operations, and environmental projects. Our team of 1,000+ engineers and scientists across the United States draw inspiration from one mission: to work closely with clients as they navigate change to create safer, more robust places to live and work. Since our founding in 1957, organizations across the public and private sectors have relied on us for technical excellence and empathetic leadership that achieve results and secure a thriving tomorrow. Learn more at haleyaldrich.com.

Haley & Aldrich is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applications will receive consideration for employment without regard to gender, race, age, disability, veteran, or any other legally protected status. We offer excellent career growth, a highly competitive total compensation plan, and a solid benefits package. Interested candidates should apply on our Careers page.

jobs.title: FERC Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Position Description

Check out what the team is up to, and what they have to offer!

https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/cd418c7ce7d846618cf14d09da16ad50

The Program Coordinator reports to the FERC License Program Manager and provides program coordination and support for the FERC License Program. This position supports the successful delivery of major programs and projects associated with ongoing FERC license compliance, as well as upcoming FERC relicensing, surrender, and transfer activities for Tacoma Power’s hydroelectric projects.

This position supports compliance with requirements established by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), including the Division of Licensing and the Division of Hydropower Administration and Compliance (DHAC), as well as internal programmatic systems and processes. The Program Coordinator assists with tracking license implementation activities, interim and formal schedules, and program milestones to support timely and compliant execution of FERC license requirements. Major tasks include developing and maintaining schedules, budgets, tracking tools, program documentation, reporting, and internal and external communications as well as identification and escalation of issues, risks, and emerging concerns.

The position supports Tacoma Power’s mission to create clean, reliable, and marketable energy while ensuring responsible stewardship of natural and cultural resources. Program activities span a broad range of resource areas, including fish and wildlife, forestry, land management, recreation, cultural resources, instream flows, water quality, and reservoir management.

The Program Coordinator plays an integral role in supporting the FERC Licensing Program and ensuring the current and future goals and obligations associated with Tacoma Power’s four hydroelectric project licenses are accomplished in a coordinated, timely, and compliant manner. The position works collaboratively across programs and disciplines within Tacoma Power to align FERC licensing and compliance activities with related operational, environmental, regulatory, and resource stewardship efforts.

Key Responsibilities

Coordinate FERC Licensing Program activities by serving as a member of the FERC Licensing Core Team and supporting coordination across relicensing, license surrender, transfer, and compliance efforts. Facilitate action-item tracking, decision documentation, communications, and alignment of critical program activities.
Develop and maintain program controls and tracking systems for FERC licensing and compliance activities, including scopes, schedules, budgets, critical paths, milestones, resource availability, risks, action items, and other program performance measures. Provide timely information and reporting to support program management and decision-making.
Coordinate project teams and advisory groups supporting Tacoma Power’s hydroelectric licenses by facilitating communication, accountability, and alignment among internal teams, consultants, contractors, agencies, and stakeholders. Identify emerging issues and support timely escalation and resolution of risks affecting program objectives.
Support FERC license compliance and regulatory requirements for Tacoma Power’s four hydroelectric projects by monitoring license obligations, reporting requirements, payments, FERC exhibits, agency and stakeholder commitments, and other compliance activities. Track license requirements and deadlines to support timely completion and reduce regulatory risk.
Coordinate meetings, communications, and program materials for senior management, internal and external teams, advisory groups, regulatory agencies, and stakeholders. Develop agendas, presentations, briefing materials, action-item records, and decision documentation to support effective program communication and governance.
Support contracts, task orders, submittals, and program documentation associated with FERC licensing, relicensing, surrender, transfer, and compliance activities. Coordinate with internal records and information management resources to maintain accurate, accessible, and appropriately controlled program documentation and ensure required FERC submittals are completed and filed on schedule.
Promote continuous improvement and professional development by identifying opportunities to improve program coordination, tracking, reporting, and information management processes; coordinating across related utility functions; and maintaining knowledge of FERC licensing and compliance practices through relevant training, conferences, and professional development.

Knowledge & Skills

Minimum Education*

Bachelor's degree in planning, engineering, architecture, project management or directly related field such as environmental science

Minimum Experience*

4 years of experience in urban planning, development, construction or inspection. Regulatory compliance or natural resources experience is preferred.

Equivalency: 1 year of experience = 1 year of education

This recruitment is being managed by Kye Merritt, if you would like to be notified of similar opportunities or stay connected with things going on at Tacoma Public Utilities and the City of Tacoma, connect with me on LinkedIn!

A Commitment to Equity & Diversity

At the City of Tacoma, we're on a mission to make our workforce as diverse and inclusive as the community we serve. We actively seek out candidates from a wide range of backgrounds and cultures. Join our team at the City of Tacoma and help us build a more vibrant, inclusive, and equitable community for all.

If you have a less traditional background, we want to hear about your transferrable skills and experience. We value a variety of perspectives and are excited to see what you bring to the table.

Tacoma is centrally located just 32 miles south of the city of Seattle and 31 miles north of the state capital, Olympia. The City of Tacoma is also home to the Port of Tacoma, which is among the largest container ports in the United States. Like most cities in the northwest, Tacoma is surrounded by beautiful nature, offering residents many opportunities for outdoor adventures.

Largely suburban in nature with a small, but dense, urban core, Tacoma is home to numerous institutes of higher learning that attract students from across the country. The University of Washington Tacoma, Pacific Lutheran University, University of Puget Sound, a satellite campus of the Evergreen State College, three community/technical colleges, and several trade and business schools are within Tacoma's geographic area. Downtown's Cultural District is the site of the Washington State History Museum, Museum of Glass, the Tacoma Art Museum, and America's Car Museum.

This position supports compliance with requirements established by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), including the Division of Licensing and the Division of Hydropower Administration and Compliance (DHAC), as well as internal programmatic systems and processes. The Program Coordinator assists with tracking license implementation activities, interim and formal schedules, and program milestones to support timely and compliant execution of FERC license requirements. Major tasks include developing and maintaining schedules, budgets, tracking tools, program documentation, reporting, and internal and external communications as well as identification and escalation of issues, risks, and emerging concerns.

The position supports Tacoma Power’s mission to create clean, reliable, and marketable energy while ensuring responsible stewardship of natural and cultural resources. Program activities span a broad range of resource areas, including fish and wildlife, forestry, land management, recreation, cultural resources, instream flows, water quality, and reservoir management.

The Program Coordinator plays an integral role in supporting the FERC Licensing Program and ensuring the current and future goals and obligations associated with Tacoma Power’s four hydroelectric project licenses are accomplished in a coordinated, timely, and compliant manner. The position works collaboratively across programs and disciplines within Tacoma Power to align FERC licensing and compliance activities with related operational, environmental, regulatory, and resource stewardship efforts.

Key Responsibilities

Coordinate FERC Licensing Program activities by serving as a member of the FERC Licensing Core Team and supporting coordination across relicensing, license surrender, transfer, and compliance efforts. Facilitate action-item tracking, decision documentation, communications, and alignment of critical program activities.
Develop and maintain program controls and tracking systems for FERC licensing and compliance activities, including scopes, schedules, budgets, critical paths, milestones, resource availability, risks, action items, and other program performance measures. Provide timely information and reporting to support program management and decision-making.
Coordinate project teams and advisory groups supporting Tacoma Power’s hydroelectric licenses by facilitating communication, accountability, and alignment among internal teams, consultants, contractors, agencies, and stakeholders. Identify emerging issues and support timely escalation and resolution of risks affecting program objectives.
Support FERC license compliance and regulatory requirements for Tacoma Power’s four hydroelectric projects by monitoring license obligations, reporting requirements, payments, FERC exhibits, agency and stakeholder commitments, and other compliance activities. Track license requirements and deadlines to support timely completion and reduce regulatory risk.
Coordinate meetings, communications, and program materials for senior management, internal and external teams, advisory groups, regulatory agencies, and stakeholders. Develop agendas, presentations, briefing materials, action-item records, and decision documentation to support effective program communication and governance.
Support contracts, task orders, submittals, and program documentation associated with FERC licensing, relicensing, surrender, transfer, and compliance activities. Coordinate with internal records and information management resources to maintain accurate, accessible, and appropriately controlled program documentation and ensure required FERC submittals are completed and filed on schedule.
Promote continuous improvement and professional development by identifying opportunities to improve program coordination, tracking, reporting, and information management processes; coordinating across related utility functions; and maintaining knowledge of FERC licensing and compliance practices through relevant training, conferences, and professional development.

Bachelor's degree in planning, engineering, architecture, project management or directly related field such as environmental science

Introduction

Are you seeking career growth within the State of Connecticut? If so, consider this new and exciting opportunity!

The S tate of Connecticut, Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP) , is currently recruiting to fill an Environmental Analyst 1 position to join our team within the Bureau of Water Protection & Land Reuse (WPLR), in Hartford, CT.

What We Can Offer You

Visit our NEW State Employee Benefits Overview page!
Professional growth and development opportunities
A healthy work/life balance to all employees
The State of Connecticut is an eligible Public Service Loan Forgiveness employer, meaning you may be eligible to have qualifying student loans forgiven after 10 years of service. Click here for more information

POSITION HIGHLIGHTS

This position is full-time, following a first shift schedule, 40 hours per week, and scheduled Monday - Friday following a hybrid work schedule.
This position in the Water Planning and Management Division, Municipal Wastewater Program.
As an Environmental Analyst 1 in this Division, you will be responsible for assisting with the management of State and Federal databases with the overarching mission of water pollution control in accordance with Federal and State laws: Clean Water Act, National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) and Sewage-Right-to-Know (SRTK) requirements.

About Us

The Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP)
is charged with conserving, improving and protecting the natural resources and the environment of the state of Connecticut as well as making cheaper, cleaner and more reliable energy available for the people and businesses of the state. The agency is also committed to playing a positive role in rebuilding Connecticut’s economy and creating jobs – and to fostering a sustainable and prosperous economic future for the state.

Within the Bureau of Water Protection & Land Reuse, the Water Planning and Management Division (WPMD)
is responsible for implementing requirements of the federal Clean Water Act and state statutes and regulations to protect water quality and habitat, ensure public health and safety, maintain water quantity, and oversee and manage critical wastewater and dam infrastructure.

The Municipal Wastewater section
handles all aspects of interactions between municipalities and DEEP regarding wastewater conveyance and treatment. From planning the needed infrastructure, through design and construction oversight, to operation, maintenance, and permitting; the Municipal Wastewater section provides holistic guidance, support, and regulatory oversight related to wastewater at the municipal level.

Job Title:
Natural Resources Programs Coordinator

Job Summary

The Natural Resources Programs Coordinator reports to the General Manager of Sealaska’s Natural Resources Department and assists in advancing various program goals for the department, including maintaining and updating program guidelines and rules and contributing to development of funding strategies, philanthropic initiatives, and emerging economic opportunities. The role is the primary writer for funding proposals and is responsible for tracking and reporting project progress in close coordination with project managers. The NR Programs Coordinator will ensure compliance with funding requirements and rules, as well as overseeing the department’s field safety protocols. A key function of the role will be to support collaborative efforts in alignment with objectives of Sealaska Corporation focused on land stewardship and economic growth in communities of Southeast Alaska. The role will be based in Sealaska’s office located in Ketchikan, AK. The role will be hybrid with a mutually agreed upon amount of both in-office presence and remote telework.

Duties/Responsibilities

Maintain a catalog of Natural Resources Department program guidelines, rules, and multi-year plans, including Sealaska’s field safety program.
Responsible for implementation and enhancement of Sealaska’s field safety protocols; includes management of safety equipment and organizing annual safety training for department staff.
Support programmatic strategic planning with the Natural Resources Department team and key partners.
Identify upcoming grant and philanthropic opportunities and maintain a grants calendar.
Prepare and submit written proposals for federal, state, philanthropic, and competitive bid opportunities.
Ensure grant compliance with organizational policies, legal requirements, and donor restrictions.
Track and monitor active project progress for internal programmatic reporting and performance reporting to funding organizations.
Works with the Sealaska Finance Department staff to track grant expenditures and review budgets against approved funding allocations.
Serve as a primary point of contact for key project partners.
Supports organizing field site visits and events to promote awareness of Sealaska’s land management mission and vision.
Build and maintain positive relationships with funding organizations and community partners.
Document creation regarding contracts and agreements with partner organizations, service providers, and funding entities.
Assists in preparation of resource management plan documents for Sealaska lands.
Occasional travel for events and site visits.
Other duties as assigned.

Required Skills/Abilities

Knowledge of federal, state, and typical philanthropic rules and requirements.
Familiar with a variety of federal, state, and philanthropic programs supporting private landowners.
Familiar with the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act; the function of Alaska Native Corporations and Tribal governments in the Southeast Alaska region.
Ability to meet and coordinate the varying work demands of natural resources professional and technical experts.
Ability to organize, direct, and carry out document production and records maintenance.
Proficient with MS Office suite and data entry.
Ability to interact diplomatically with Sealaska shareholders, visiting professionals, and the general public.
Ability to perform independent research and read and interpret laws, regulations, technical reports.
Possess an advanced level of communication, reasoning, problem solving and interpersonal skills necessary to perform essential functions of the job.
Excellent report writing and grant writing skills.
Excellent organizational and planning skills with attention to detail.
Ability to work in a team setting.
Ability to organize events and meetings.

Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree preferred, not required.
5 or more years grant administration experience. The career level of the position will be determined by the years of relevant experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities.

Working Conditions

The physical and work environment characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Physical Demands

Physical demand requirements are more than those for sedentary work.
The employee exerts up to 30 pounds of force occasionally and/or up to 10 pounds of force frequently, and/or negligible amount of force constantly to move objects.
The employee is frequently required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to handle or feel and reach with hands and arms.
The employee is occasionally required to stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.
Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and distance vision.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear.
Comfortable with occasional travel in utility task vehicles, small planes, and marine vessels.
The noise level in the work environment is usually quiet to moderate.

Work Environment

This position will be occasionally required to work outdoors of a wet and temperate climate, and at times may include walking and hiking several miles while carrying equipment weighing approximately 30 lbs.

This description is not intended to be, nor should it be construed as an all-inclusive list of responsibilities, skills or working conditions associated with the position. It is intended to accurately reflect the activities and requirements of the position, but duties may be added, deleted, or modified, as necessary. This description does not constitute a written or implied contract of employment.

Review the Benefits associated with this position: https://www.sealaska.com/benefits/

Sealaska and its affiliates do not make job offers without first conducting live in-person or virtual interviews, and they do not conduct interviews by email/text. Please be sure to confirm the legitimacy of all job postings on the sealska.com careers page
and https://jobs.dayforcehcm.com/en-US/sealaska/CANDIDATEPORTAL careers site before sharing any of your personal information.

Established in 1972, Sealaska is the Alaska Native regional corporation for Southeast Alaska.
